resolutions.researcher_notes: Possible other name for P7802, Tennessee Gas Pipeline, Mississippi Crossing (MSX). Kinder Morgan's project page and a Pipeline & Gas Journal article from December 2024 call this project the "Mississippi Crossing Project": about 208 miles of 42 and 36 inch pipe from near Greenville, Mississippi, to near Butler, Alabama, up to 2.1 Bcf/d. That matches this row, so it is very likely the same project, but check before accepting. Row P7841 already uses this name as its pipeline name, and it is flagged separately as a likely duplicate of this row. If P7841 is removed, this keeps the name on P7802. Accepting adds the name to the other English names cell and changes nothing else. The other English names column has no reference column, so the sources are listed here. Pages that use the name: https://kindermorgan.com/Operations/Projects/Mississippi-Crossing-Project; https://pgjonline.com/news/2024/december/kinder-morgan-approves-14-billion-mississippi-crossing-project-to-boost-southeast-gas-supply.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Possible other name for P7792, Transcontinental Gas Pipeline, Southeast Energy Connector Project. The EIA natural gas pipeline projects workbook listed this project as "Southeast Energy Corridor Project" in its releases from October 2022 through April 2024, then renamed it Southeast Energy Connector Project from July 2024 on. Both names carry the same FERC docket, CP22-501, and the same 1.9 miles of 42 inch pipe and 150 MMcf/d in Alabama, so it is the same project. The older name may be EIA's own spelling and not a name Transco used. A web search for the exact older name found no other page. It is worth keeping only to help match old EIA lists, so decide whether it belongs. Accepting adds the name to the other English names cell and changes nothing else. The other English names column has no reference column, so the source is listed here. Page that uses the name: https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects_Apr2024.xlsx.
